active_family: native joint conditional generator for IV + anchor factors; 656a empirical-copula deck retained only as a diagnostic stress-deck baseline
current_bottleneck: Post-hoc composition is not methodologically satisfying for the long-term objective. 656a fixes the 574a diagonal-rank artifact and shows that mixed IV/factor rank states can be preserved, but IV and factors are still generated by different mechanisms and paired afterward. That is hard to justify as a generalizable conditional scenario generator.
last_result_summary: 656a added empirical-copula pairing for the IV + anchor-factor stress deck. It estimates the pre-deck historical rank copula between 30-day IV severity and anchor-factor stress over 5763 windows, samples factor stress ranks conditional on selected IV severity bucket, and selects generated panel-law factor paths by factor stress rank. The generated 48-scenario deck matches historical mixed bucket behavior: selected_mixed_bucket_rate=0.520833 versus historical_mixed_bucket_rate=0.5249, selected_rank_corr=0.478231 versus historical_rank_corr=0.457686. After review, this should be treated as a diagnostic/falsification baseline, not a promoted core methodology, because factors and IV are not born from one shared conditional mechanism.
next_step_recommendation: Do not promote 656a as the final deployable/publishable path. Keep it as evidence that diagonal same-rank pairing is too restrictive. The next principled move is a native joint generator: one model state, one stochastic source, all IV and anchor-factor channels generated together, with type-aware preprocessing/readouts only for unit/support differences.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 612a is the highest IV-count native joint run at 6/11 but has a degenerate source-scale mechanism and poor anchor-factor joint audit. 656a is a better diagnostic stress-deck overlay than 574a because it preserves historical mixed IV/factor rank behavior instead of forcing same-rank pairing, but it is still a composed deck and should not be promoted as the core generalizable model. 641a/652a are the cleaner native joint baselines because they remove post-hoc gluing, but they are still not IV-deployable.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
